# Project sessions: projects made of forge repositories, opened as one session

## What to build

A **project** (KAN-95, multi-repo) is today a named group of existing local clones (workspace ids) of one forge, with a folder `<GM_WORKSPACES_DIR>/.projects/<id>/` made when the project is created. The Workspaces tab is gone, so projects must now be built from **forge repositories** and cloned only when a **project session** starts. This task:

1. stores a project's repositories as `repos: RepoRef[]` instead of workspace ids (existing projects are migrated from their workspace ids when they are read);
2. makes `POST /api/projects` / `PATCH /api/projects/:id` take `repos: RepoRef[]`, and stops creating the project folder at create time;
3. lets `WorkspaceHost.prepare` take `{ project: { id, name?, repos } }`: it clones or updates every repository on the same new or existing branch and writes the project folder exactly as `routes/projects.ts` does today (`project.json`, `repos/<name>` links, its own git repo); `changes`, `save` and `discard` act on every repository of the project;
4. lets `POST /api/sessions { projectId, branch, agent? }` open a project session: one session (counting as one toward `GM_MAX_SESSIONS`), one terminal whose cwd is the project folder with `GM_PROJECT_ID` set;
5. changes the Projects page and `ProjectDialog` to pick repositories from the forge search (`GET /api/repos`), and makes **Open terminal** open a project session through the New terminal dialog, which lists projects.

Do not change anything in `packages/graph-execution` (the engine).

## What already exists (built by earlier tasks; read the code, do not rebuild it)

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/types.ts`: `RepoRef = { forge: "github" | "gitlab"; owner: string; name: string; baseUrl?: string }` and `WorkspaceHost` with `prepare(p: { repo: RepoRef; branch: { new: string } | { existing: string } }): Promise<{ workspaceId: string; branch: string }>`, `spawnPty`, `startEngine`, `readFile`, `listFiles`, `listRuns`, `runDetail`, `git`, `activity`, `changes(workspaceId): Promise<string[]>`, `save({ workspaceId, branch, message }): Promise<{ pushed; skipped; error? }>`, `discard(workspaceId)`, `loginFiles`, and possibly `pushBranch(workspaceId)` (hosted-runs task).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/local.ts` `LocalWorkspaceHost`: `prepare` clones a missing repository into `<workspacesDir>/<forge>/<owner…>/<name>` (workspace id `<forge>~<owner…>~<name>`), else fetches and checks out the branch, and refuses with 409 `{"error":"acme/api has uncommitted changes. Close its session with Push or Discard first."}` when the clone is dirty and the branch differs. Find its helper that turns a `RepoRef` into a workspace id / path (grep `local.ts` and `host/types.ts`), and use it; if there is none, add `export function workspaceIdOf(repo: RepoRef): string` (`[repo.forge, ...repo.owner.split("/"), repo.name].join("~")`) and `repoRefOf(workspaceId: string): RepoRef | undefined` (the inverse: first part the forge, last part the name, the middle joined with `/` the owner; undefined when the forge is not github/gitlab or there are fewer than 3 parts) to `host/types.ts`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/contract.ts` exports `hostContractSuite(name, makeHost)`, run against `LocalWorkspaceHost` and against `RemoteWorkspaceHost` talking to a local `graph-manager agent` process (`src/server/agent/server.ts`, `src/server/host/remote.ts`). The agent serves `prepare` under `/agent/v1/*`: check its body schema accepts the project form too.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/sessions.ts` (`SessionManager`) and `src/server/routes/sessions.ts`: `POST /api/sessions` with `{ repo } | { projectId }` plus `{ branch: { new?: string } | { existing: string }, agent?, cols?, rows? }` → `201 { sessionId, terminalId, branch }`; the `GM_MAX_SESSIONS` 409 `{"error":"You have 3 open repositories. Close all terminals of one to open another."}`; the session record `{ id, repo, workspaceId, branch, state, startedAt, error? }` in the user's store (`Data.sessions`); `provisioner.acquire({ user, sessionId })` → host. Read how a repo session is opened there (`SessionManager.open`: cap check inside one `us.update` → `provisioner.acquire` → `host.prepare` → login files / agent keys → `openTerminal(user, { host, workspaceId, cwd, agent, cols, rows, title, sessionId, env })`) and add the project branch next to it; the `projectId` form currently answers 400 `{"error":"project sessions are not supported yet"}` — replace that. `GET /api/repos?q=` answers `{ repos: Array<{ repo: RepoRef, fullPath, defaultBranch, private, webUrl, live, sessionId?, branch? }>, forges: { github: boolean, gitlab: boolean } }`; `GET /api/repos/branches?forge=&owner=&name=` → `{ defaultBranch, branches }`.
- The New terminal dialog (`src/web/pages/NewTerminalDialog.tsx`, terminal-ui task) lists live sessions, projects (`data-testid="new-terminal-project-<id>"`) and repositories, and posts `POST /api/sessions { projectId, branch, agent? }` for a project. `Terminals.tsx` handles `?project=<id>[&agent=]` by opening the dialog with that project preselected. The sidebar groups terminals by session (`TerminalSidebar.tsx` `groupTerminals(terminals, sessions, projects)`), labelling a session with `projectId` by the project's name (`src/web/sessions.ts` `sessionLabel`). Verify each of these in the code; finish whatever is missing for projects.
- State is per user: `const us = await ctx.store.forUser(req.user)`; `us.get()` / `us.update(fn)`. Never `ctx.store.get()`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts` (the `projects` field of the data schema, today lines 101–104: `z.record(z.string(), z.object({ name, workspaces: z.array(z.string()), createdAt }))`, and the `projects()` / `project(id)` helpers, today lines 163–173; the earlier db task may have moved these — grep `projects` in `store.ts` and `db/`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/projects.ts` (whole file, 229 lines): `Project` (lines 15–22), `repoNamesOf` (55–76), `writeProjectFile` (133–146), `createProjectFolder` (148–171), `syncProjectFolder` (177–213), `removeProjectFolder` (215–229).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.ts` (whole file, 160 lines): `ProjectView` (20–30), `checkWorkspaces` (37–51), `viewOf` (53–71), the routes (83–159).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runhome.ts` (lines 18–28 `projectHome`, 31–38 `resolveRunHome`, 66–78 `projectRepos`) and `src/server/project-pr.ts` (line 119) — consumers of `project.workspaces` (workspace ids). Keep them working.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` (lines 40–104, today's `projectId` handling: cwd = `projectDirOf(...)`, `GM_PROJECT_ID` env, title = project name, Qwen's project-config into the project folder) — the behaviour a project session's terminal must keep.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.test.ts` (lines 1–60 setup with `appWithLogin()` and temp git repos; tests at 44–290) and `src/server/projects.test.ts` — tests to adapt.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/ProjectDialog.tsx` (whole file, 148 lines), `src/web/pages/Projects.tsx` (lines 28–60 state, 95–210 table and empty states, 230–250 dialog and delete confirm), `src/web/pages/Projects.test.tsx` (lines 1–137 setup, tests at 138–320), `src/web/types.ts` (`ProjectEntry`, lines 90–100), `src/web/useProjects.ts` (`projectList`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Runs.tsx` line 337 (`p.workspaces.map((w) => w.repo)`) and `src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx` (project handling) — consumers of `ProjectEntry.workspaces`; keep that field in the API view.
- `docs/prd/hosted-sessions.md` "Requirements → WorkspaceHost" last bullet and the "Project sessions" decision.

## Patterns to follow

**Schema migration on read (zod preprocess), as `sandboxRecipe` does with `migrateRecipe` in `store.ts`:**
```ts
const projectRecord = z.preprocess(
  migrateProject, // { name, workspaces: string[], createdAt } → { name, repos: RepoRef[], createdAt }; ids that do not parse are dropped
  z.object({ name: z.string(), repos: z.array(repoRefSchema), createdAt: z.string() }),
);
projects: z.record(z.string(), projectRecord).default({}),
```
`repoRefSchema = z.object({ forge: z.enum(["github", "gitlab"]), owner: z.string().min(1), name: z.string().min(1), baseUrl: z.string().url().optional() })`. Because the store keeps each user's `Data` as one JSON document validated by this schema, the migration applies to every user's data whatever the database.

**Keep the derived workspace ids for the code that needs local paths.** `Project` becomes:
```ts
export interface Project {
  id: string; name: string;
  repos: RepoRef[];
  /** Derived: `repos.map(workspaceIdOf)`, the local clone ids (runhome.ts, project-pr.ts use them). */
  workspaces: string[];
  createdAt: string;
}
```
Build it in one place (the store's `projects()` / `project(id)` helpers, or a `projectOf(id, rec)` function in `projects.ts`) so `runhome.ts`, `project-pr.ts` and project runs need no change.

**Route errors:** `reply.code(400).send({ error: "…" })`; zod bodies with `.strict()` as today (`routes/projects.ts` 32–33).

**Server tests:** `appWithLogin()` and `app.inject`, temp bare git remotes for clones (the sessions task's `sessions.test.ts` has a helper that makes a bare remote and a fake forge connection — reuse it), `execa("git", …)` to inspect results.

**Web tests:** jsdom + Testing Library with a stubbed `fetch`, as `Projects.test.tsx` 1–137.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/types.ts` and `host/local.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `prepare`'s parameter becomes `{ repo: RepoRef; branch: … } | { project: { id: string; name?: string; repos: RepoRef[] }; branch: … }` (update the interface, `LocalWorkspaceHost`, `RemoteWorkspaceHost` in `host/remote.ts` and the agent's handler/schema in `src/server/agent/server.ts`, which just forwards to its `LocalWorkspaceHost`).
- Local project prepare:
  1. Resolve the branch name once: `{ new: name }` → that name for every repository; `{ existing: b }` → `b`.
  2. For each repository, do exactly what the single-repo prepare does (clone if missing, else fetch and check out the branch; the 409 dirty-clone message names that repository). If one fails, throw that error (the clones already done stay; nothing is rolled back).
  3. Write the project folder with `createProjectFolder(workspacesDir, project, workspaces)` when `<workspacesDir>/.projects/<id>` does not exist, else `syncProjectFolder(...)` (both in `src/server/projects.ts`; they take `Workspace[]` from `resolveWorkspace(workspacesDir, workspaceIdOf(repo))` and a `Project` with `name` — use `name ?? id`).
  4. Return `{ workspaceId: "project~<id>", branch }` (`PROJECT_PREFIX` from `runhome.ts`).
- `changes("project~<id>")`: the union of every repository's changes, each line prefixed with its `repos/` name (`api/src/x.ts`; use the names in the folder's `project.json` via `readProjectFile`). `save({ workspaceId: "project~<id>", branch, message })`: save every repository to `branch`; `pushed` is true only if all pushed; `skipped` prefixed the same way; `error` = the failing repositories' errors joined with `; `, each as `<repo>: <error>`. `discard("project~<id>")`: discard in every repository. `git`, `readFile`, `listFiles`, `spawnPty`, `startEngine`, `listRuns`, `runDetail` on `project~<id>` work on the project folder (that is how project runs and terminals work today through `resolveRunHome`; check what `local.ts` already does for `project~` ids and keep it). If `pushBranch` exists, on `project~<id>` it pushes every repository's branch.
- **GOTCHA**: the project folder is a local git repo with no remote; never `save`/`push` it. Its repos are links under `repos/` to the real clones; work on the clones (resolve by workspace id), not through the links.
- **GOTCHA**: `syncProjectFolder` keeps link names by where links point; keep calling it rather than rewriting the folder, so names stay stable across sessions.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- host agent`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/contract.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add a project case to `hostContractSuite` (so it runs against both the local host and the agent): two temp bare remotes `octo/api` and `octo/web`; `prepare({ project: { id: "billing", name: "billing", repos: [api, web] }, branch: { new: "gm/test-1" } })` → `{ workspaceId: "project~billing", branch: "gm/test-1" }`; both clones are on `gm/test-1`; `readFile("project~billing", "project.json")` lists `api` and `web` with paths `repos/api`, `repos/web`; a new file in `api` shows in `changes` as `api/<file>`; `save` pushes both repositories' branch to their remotes; `discard` cleans both.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- contract host agent`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts` and `src/server/projects.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: the `projects` record holds `{ name, repos: RepoRef[], createdAt }` with the `migrateProject` preprocess above (an old record `{ name, workspaces: ["github~octo~api", "github~octo~web"], createdAt }` reads as `repos: [{ forge: "github", owner: "octo", name: "api" }, …]`; GitLab subgroups: `gitlab~grp~sub~proj` → `{ forge: "gitlab", owner: "grp/sub", name: "proj" }`). `Project` gains `repos` and keeps the derived `workspaces`. The store helpers (or `projectOf`) return the derived field. `repoNamesOf` keeps taking `Workspace[]`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- store projects`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Bodies: `createBody = z.object({ name: z.string().trim(), repos: z.array(repoRefSchema) }).strict()`, `patchBody = z.object({ repos: z.array(repoRefSchema) }).strict()`.
  - `checkRepos(repos)` replaces `checkWorkspaces`: no repository twice → 400 `{"error":"a repository is listed twice"}`; fewer than 2 → 400 `{"error":"a project needs at least 2 repositories"}`; two forges → 400 `{"error":"all repositories of a project must come from one forge"}`. No clone and no forge call here.
  - `POST /api/projects`: same name rules and 409 as today (lines 87–95); stores the record; **no folder is created** (the folder is written by `prepare` when a session starts). 201 with the view.
  - `PATCH /api/projects/:id`: 404 as today; 409 `{"error":"a run of this project is live"}` as today; new: 409 `{"error":"project <name> has a live session. Close it first."}` when the user has a session whose `workspaceId` is `project~<id>`. Stores the new repos; if the folder exists and every repository has a local clone, `syncProjectFolder` it (else leave it for the next session).
  - `DELETE /api/projects/:id`: as today (live run 409, remove its terminals, `removeProjectFolder` if the folder exists, delete the record), plus the same live-session 409.
  - `ProjectView` adds `repos: RepoRef[]` and keeps `workspaces: { id, fullPath, repo }[]` built from the derived ids (`fullPath` = `owner/name`, `repo` from `project.json` when the folder exists, else from `repoNamesOf`-style naming of the last path segment). `forge` = `repos[0]?.forge ?? ""`.
  - Use `const us = await ctx.store.forUser(req.user)` for every read and write.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- routes/projects`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/sessions.ts` and `src/server/sessions/sessions.ts` — project sessions

- **IMPLEMENT** the `{ projectId }` form of `POST /api/sessions`:
  - unknown project (in the user's store) → 404 `{"error":"project not found"}`;
  - a live session whose `workspaceId` is `project~<projectId>` → a new terminal in it (branch ignored) → 201 `{ sessionId, terminalId, branch }`, like a live repository;
  - else: the same `GM_MAX_SESSIONS` check (a project session counts as one), `provisioner.acquire({ user, sessionId })`, `host.prepare({ project: { id, name, repos }, branch })`, then the same login-files / agent-keys steps as a repository session, then the terminal: cwd = the project folder, env `GM_PROJECT_ID=<id>` (as `routes/terminals.ts` does today), title = project name (or `<Agent label> · <project name>` for an agent), and for an agent with `connect === "project-config"` (Qwen Code) the config is written into the project folder's own repo, as `routes/terminals.ts` 85–94 does.
  - The session record gets `projectId?: string` and `repos?: RepoRef[]`; `repo` is the first repository (keeps the type required); `GET /api/sessions` returns `projectId`.
  - The default new branch name is the same `gm/<user-id>-<yyyymmdd>-<4 random chars>` the repository flow uses (reuse its helper).
  - Closing (`asking` / push / keep / discard / `save-failed` / idle backup) needs no project-specific code once `changes`/`save`/`discard` handle `project~<id>`; check the dialog text uses the project name: the label the UI shows comes from `sessionLabel`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- routes/sessions sessions`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/types.ts`, `src/web/useProjects.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `ProjectEntry` gains `repos: RepoRef[]` (keep `workspaces`). `projectList` accepts both an array and `{ projects: [...] }` as today.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/ProjectDialog.tsx`

- **IMPLEMENT**: drop the `workspaces` prop. The Repositories fieldset gets a search input (`data-testid="project-repo-search"`, placeholder `Search repositories`) querying `GET /api/repos?q=<q>` (debounced 200 ms) and a result list (`data-testid="project-repo-results"`) of checkboxes, one per entry of `repos` (use `entry.repo` as the `RepoRef`; `data-testid="project-repo-<forge>-<owner>/<name>"`, label `fullPath` + `ForgeChip`). With both `forges` false, show "Connect GitHub or GitLab in Settings first." Picked repositories show above the search as removable chips in the order picked (`data-testid="project-picked"`), so a pick survives a new search. Once one is picked, results of the other forge are hidden; the hint says `Only <forge> repositories: a project uses one forge connection.` / `Pick at least two repositories of one forge.`. Edit mode starts with the project's `repos`. Save posts `{ name, repos }` (new) or `PATCH { repos }` (edit). Show the server error as today.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- pages/Projects`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Projects.tsx`

- **IMPLEMENT**: stop reading `overview.workspaces`. Empty state: with no forge connected (`useOverview().forges`), "Connect GitHub or GitLab first" with a link to `/settings`; else "No projects yet" with the New project button and the body "A project groups repositories of one forge in one folder, for specs, tasks and runs across them." Repo chips come from `repos` (`owner/name` as title, the `repo` name from `workspaces` when present, else `name`). The agent buttons and **Terminal** navigate to `/terminals?project=<id>&agent=<agent>` / `/terminals?project=<id>`, which open the New terminal dialog with the project preselected (branch and agent are chosen there). A project with a live session shows a `live` badge (`data-testid="project-live-<id>"`, from `useOverview().sessions`). Footer note: "Deleting a project removes its folder only. The clones stay." Delete confirm body: "This removes the project folder <path> with its specs, tasks and runs. The clones stay."
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- pages/Projects`

### UPDATE the New terminal dialog and the sidebar (only what is missing)

- Check `src/web/pages/NewTerminalDialog.tsx`: projects are listed from `/api/projects` (name + repo count + projects icon), filtered by the query (name or any repo `owner/name`); a project with a live session is listed once, as the live entry, with a `live` badge; picking a project shows the branch row (New/Existing; Existing lists the branches of the project's first repository via `/api/repos/branches?forge=&owner=&name=`) and posts `POST /api/sessions { projectId, branch, agent? }`; picking a live project session posts `POST /api/sessions/:id/terminals`. `?project=<id>[&agent=]` preselects it.
- Check `TerminalSidebar.tsx`: a project session section shows the projects icon and the project's name.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- pages/Terminals`

### TESTS

- `src/server/store.test.ts` (or `projects.test.ts`): an old record with `workspaces: ["github~octo~api", "github~octo~web"]` reads as `repos` `[{forge:"github",owner:"octo",name:"api"}, …]`; `gitlab~grp~sub~proj` → owner `grp/sub`; the derived `workspaces` equals the old ids.
- `routes/projects.test.ts`: rewrite for `repos` bodies: bad name / twice / fewer than 2 / two forges with the exact messages above; create does not make a folder; list returns `repos` and `workspaces`; PATCH and DELETE answer 409 with the live-session message while a project session is live; a live run still blocks as today; another user's project is 404 (two users through the accounts helper the earlier tasks added).
- `routes/sessions.test.ts` (or a new `project-sessions.test.ts`): with two temp bare remotes and `LocalProvisioner`, `POST /api/sessions { projectId: "billing", branch: { new: "gm/x" } }` → 201; both clones exist on `gm/x`; `.projects/billing/project.json` lists both repos and the folder is its own git repo; the terminal's cwd is the project folder and its env has `GM_PROJECT_ID=billing`; a second POST joins the same session; with `GM_MAX_SESSIONS=1` a repository session after it answers the 409 message (the project counted as one); closing the last terminal with a change in one repository answers `ask.changes` with `api/<file>`, and `push` pushes that repository's branch.
- `host/contract.ts`: the project case above (runs for local and remote hosts).
- `src/web/pages/Projects.test.tsx`: New project searches `/api/repos?q=`, picks two GitHub repositories (GitLab results hide after the first pick), posts `{ name, repos: [ … ] }` in pick order; Edit repos starts with the project's repos and PATCHes `{ repos }`; the Terminal button goes to `/terminals?project=billing`; the empty state without a forge links to Settings; replace the old "asks for two workspaces first" test.
- `src/web/pages/Terminals.test.tsx`: `?project=billing&agent=claude` opens the dialog with the project and Claude preselected; Open posts `POST /api/sessions` with `{ projectId: "billing", branch: { new: … }, agent: "claude" }`.

### CHECK in a real browser (TESTING.md: UI changes must be looked at)

Build and start as TESTING.md "graph-manager" describes, with the fake forge; add a second GitHub repository to the fake forge (the `addRepo` helper of `scripts/fake-forge.mjs`, or `startFakeForge` in a small script), connect GitHub with `gh-good`. With agent-browser: Projects → New project → search, pick `octo/hello` and the second repository → Create; the row shows both chips and no folder exists yet under `$GM_DIR/ws/.projects/`; Terminal → the New terminal dialog has the project picked → New branch → Open; the sidebar shows one section with the project's name; `$GM_DIR/ws/.projects/<id>/project.json` lists both repos and both clones are on the session branch. Restart the server after each build; use free ports; stop servers by PID.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Projects store `repos: RepoRef[]`; an existing project stored with workspace ids reads as the same repositories.
- [ ] `POST /api/projects { name, repos }` and `PATCH /api/projects/:id { repos }` validate with the exact messages above and do not clone or make a folder.
- [ ] `POST /api/sessions { projectId, branch }` opens one session with every repository cloned on the same branch, the project folder written (`project.json`, `repos/<name>` links, its own git repo), a terminal in the project folder with `GM_PROJECT_ID`; a second terminal joins it; it counts as one session toward `GM_MAX_SESSIONS`.
- [ ] `changes`, `save` and `discard` act on every repository of a project session; the close dialog lists `<repo>/<file>` paths.
- [ ] The host contract suite covers a project and passes for the local host and the agent.
- [ ] New project / Edit repos pick repositories from the forge search; Open terminal opens a project session from the New terminal dialog; the dialog lists projects.
- [ ] Another user's projects are 404 / absent.
- [ ] `packages/graph-execution` is unchanged.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test -w graph-manager -- projects sessions host contract agent store pages/Projects pages/Terminals`

## Validation commands

```bash
# Type / lint
npm run typecheck && npm run lint

# Tests for this slice
npm test -w graph-manager -- projects sessions host contract agent store pages/Projects pages/Terminals project-pr project-runs runhome

# Everything in graph-manager, and the engine untouched
npm test -w graph-manager
git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution   # must print nothing
```
